body:
## Problem / motivation

The bounded Guardian review undertaken alongside phase 6.3 / #282 has evidence for ordinary integer and UUID primary keys, exact configured permission keys (including tested Unicode variants), preservation of supplied queryset scope/model/database alias, and configured content-type behavior. The relevant database fixtures use SQLite, including independent `default` and `shard` aliases.

That evidence does not establish identity preservation for arbitrary custom primary-key fields, database casts, or collations on other backends. Track those cases as a separate compatibility investigation with an explicit support matrix and observable acceptance criteria.

No precision defect has been demonstrated by this review. The original planning detector's generic precision prompt was triggered by the word “boundary” in unrelated adjacent prose; it was not a runtime finding. The subsequent plan nevertheless recorded a permission-identity review obligation. This issue gives the broader, unverified cases a concrete follow-up destination without claiming that they pass or that existing supported behavior is broken.

## Proposed solution

Define and verify a bounded Guardian identity contract:

> Within each explicitly supported configuration, assigning an object permission and querying permitted objects must preserve the intended model/content-type and object identity under the declared field/backend equality semantics. The integration must preserve supplied queryset restrictions and the intended database alias, and must not introduce lossy permission-key normalization or broaden access through unintended identity conversion.

Start with a documented support decision, then add discriminating integration tests:

- Choose named database backends, versions and collations to investigate. PostgreSQL and MySQL/MariaDB are candidates, not support promises made by this issue.
- Choose representative custom primary-key fields and representations based on intended support. Candidate cases include text keys with leading zeros, case differences, distinct Unicode representations, integer range boundaries, and custom field conversion hooks.
- State which values are distinct under each selected field/backend configuration before asserting results. Do not assume that every collation treats case or Unicode forms identically.
- Exercise real permission assignment, lookup and removal, plus helper/list/object access as applicable. Seed granted and ungranted neighboring identities; assert both positive access and exclusion controls. Retain user/group, inactive-user, strict-helper and per-view global-fallback policy expectations.
- Preserve supplied queryset model, scope and alias. Characterize unsupported combinations and record an explicit support restriction or a separate concrete defect with a reproduction.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Publish a finite PK/backend/collation matrix and the intended identity/equality rule for each supported row.
- [ ] Add real database integration tests proving both correct access and absence of access to distinct ungranted identities in that matrix.
- [ ] Verify permission-key handling, content-type selection, queryset restrictions and alias preservation without changing established actor policies.
- [ ] Document tested support and known limitations; record untested combinations as unverified.
- [ ] Fix any reproduced package defect with a regression test and appropriate release/migration documentation, or explicitly track it separately.
- [ ] Keep ordinary integer/UUID/exact-key regressions passing.

## Alternatives considered

- Claim universal precision from the existing SQLite tests: insufficient evidence.
- Leave an undefined precision obligation open indefinitely: replace it with the finite contract and matrix above.
- Require support for every custom field/backend combination: impractical; scope must be explicit and evidence-backed.

## Scope and relationship to phase 6.3

This is follow-up validation and compatibility work for `crud_views_guardian`. The existing phase 6.3 evidence remains bounded to the tested cases. Filing this issue does not itself mark the broader guarantee verified, change package-wide database support, complete phase 6.3, or close #282.

Centralized authorization across separate databases is a separate architecture/support question. This issue does not promise or implement that topology; split out a dedicated issue if it is required. Existing same-alias behavior and conservative unsupported-topology handling must remain intact.

Development evidence is on branch `introduce-gsd` (investigation baseline `0cb9f57`), including:

- `tests/test1/test_guardian_policy.py`
- `tests/test1/test_guardian_content_types.py`
- `tests/test1/test_delete_databases.py`
- `.planning/phases/06.3-delete-protection-and-write-boundary-integrity-issue-282/06.3-GUARDIAN-REVIEW.md`

These development-branch references are not a claim that the work has already shipped on the default branch.

## Affected area

crud_views_guardian
